recorded: Every case passed 10 runs against the original with Node.js 26.12.1, fastify 5.7.4, @fastify/jwt 10.0.0, @fastify/rate-limit 10.3.0, and mongodb 7.1.0, run as node src/index.js, the file npm start runs, with DB_NAME from the cases instead of npm start's customers, and with MongoDB 9.0.4 from the module's compose file, the mongo image at latest, under a container name of its own and published on port 48836, where DB_PORT points the API. Each case names a database of its own in DB_NAME, so the cases share no data, the services start empty on every run, and the service tokens and rate limit counts, kept in the API's memory, start empty with every case. The JWTs the login issues carry the second they were signed and the service tokens are random UUIDs, so both are checked by shape and sent back in later requests. The JWTs the cases sign by hand use HS256, the secret supersecret, and an iat of 1767225600, and the expired one an exp a minute later. The rate limit cases spend 90 requests by repeating one request, check x-ratelimit-reset and retry-after as 50 to 60 seconds, and the 429's wait as 1 minute or a number of seconds. The runner's readiness check calls /v1/health once without a token, which counts toward the caller's address, so no case compares that address's count exactly. ObjectIds are generated, so the cases check 24 lowercase hex digits and compare later answers with the ids the API returned. Validation messages come from Ajv, so they are checked by status and the presence of a message, while the unknown route's message is compared exactly. No case deletes a well-formed id that matches nothing, since the original never answers it.

services.up:
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f - -p stackfy-08-publishing-crud up -d --wait mongodb <<'EOF'
services:
  mongodb:
    container_name: stackfy-08-publishing-crud-mongodb
    ports: !override ['48836:27017']
EOF

cases.name: answers its health to anyone with the app's name and version, CORS headers, and the rate limit of the caller's address, and answers every other request without a valid token with 401 Unauthorized and neither CORS nor rate limit headers, unknown routes, preflights, and the health with a query included

expect.pattern: Connected to the database\nserver is running at http://\S+:48835\n

cases.name: refuses to start without DB_NAME, printing its error and exiting 1

expect.pattern: \[error\*{5}\]: please, pass DB_NAME env before running it!\n

cases.name: logs in with a username in any case and its password, answering a JWT the API accepts after Bearer in any case but not alone, lets the admin write and the member only read, checks a body before the role, and refuses wrong credentials with 401 and a missing password with Fastify's 400 body

accepts any JWT signed with HS256 and the secret supersecret, trusting the username and role it claims without looking them up, compares the role exactly, and refuses a JWT signed with another secret, an expired one, and one whose algorithm is none

issues a random UUID as a service token, with the role, to known credentials only when adminSuperSecret is AM I THE BOSS?, checked first, accepts it after Bearer in any case or alone until the server stops, refuses a token it never issued, and answers an unknown route or a preflight once the token is accepted

counts 90 requests a minute for each token, refusals and reads alike, and answers the next with 429, @fastify/rate-limit's body, and a retry-after but no CORS headers, on every route, the health included, while another token keeps its own count

cases.name: counts the requests without a token by the caller address, the login, the service token route, and the health alike, so a login tried too often answers 429 even with the right password, while a token keeps its own count

cases.name: creates customers under a new ObjectId, rejects a body without a phone with Fastify's 400 body, and lists them by name as MongoDB compares bytes, with the fields a body brought beyond the schema, all as the admin after logging in
finds a customer by its ObjectId with only id, name, and phone, answers an unknown one with an empty 404 body, and rejects ids that are not 24 hex digits, all as the admin after logging in
replaces a name and a phone, answers 404 when nothing changes or the id is unknown, and 400 for a malformed id or a body without a phone, all as the admin after logging in
